payload.task_text:
I need to review our product ratings and set up a feedback process for our underperforming products. Please look at all products in our store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.

For these five lowest-rated products, create a Google Form titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with a sheet called Review Summary that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns for Product_Name truncated to sixty characters, Avg_Rating rounded to two decimal places, Review_Count, and Category using the first category name from each product. Sort by Avg_Rating in ascending order. Add a second sheet called Stats with Metric and Value rows for Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product with the product name truncated to forty characters, and Avg_Rating_Overall as the average rating across all reviewed products rounded to two decimal places. Write all numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) as literal numbers, not spreadsheet formulas.

Schedule a product quality review meeting in the calendar on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm with the title Product Quality Review Meeting.

Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one read-only Explore wave for the 82-product/396-review store join, then one writer wave with two parallel coder sub-agents. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload between the waves is the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace and freeze the ranking contract: every product with at least one review, ranked by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID; the five lowest define the survey, meeting and email. Start the fixed-date event inventory independently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent (read-only):

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Review gatherer: paginate both store endpoints with perPage=100 and increasing page until a short or empty page, omitting review status and preserving observed statuses. Join strictly on Product_ID; for every product with at least one review compute the literal Review_Count and the average rating (full precision, 2-decimal display), keeping the full product name and the first category. Select the lowest five by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return only the complete reviewed-products table (id, full name, avg_rating, review_count, first category), the frozen five-row ranking with complete product names, record counts, duplicate IDs, and page controls — no writes, no full item arrays.

After Wave 1, verify the handoff in one single pass: row count equals the product join, every reviewed product covered, five-row ranking unambiguous. The main agent then freezes one canonical product_review_data.json in the workspace containing: the products list (82 objects with id, full name, avg_rating 2 decimals, review_count, category), the frozen bottom-five ranking with complete names, and the Stats values (Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product truncated to forty characters, Avg_Rating_Overall rounded to two decimals). This file is the single binding input for Wave 2; nobody re-reads the store afterwards.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming product_review_data.json verbatim with no recomputation and no store reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Review Summary with columns Product_Name (truncated to sixty characters), Avg_Rating (two decimals), Review_Count, Category (first category), one row per reviewed product sorted by Avg_Rating ascending; Stats with columns Metric, Value and rows Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (truncated to forty characters), Avg_Rating_Overall (two decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, never formulas; read both populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External writer — sole owner of form, event and email. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with the stated description, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially on that one formId five add_multiple_choice_question calls in frozen rank order, each using the product name in the question text with options ["1","2","3","4","5"] and required=true, followed by one add_text_question(..., required=false) for additional suggestions; call get_form and verify title/description/question order/types/options/flags. Filter list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime") locally for the exact Product Quality Review Meeting at 14:00-15:00; create it once only if missing with exact start.dateTime/end.dateTime, retain the ID, and call get_event. Paginate Sent search for product.team@company.com and exact subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required, send at most once naming the frozen five products, then read it back.

After Wave 2, verify both handoffs in one single pass against product_review_data.json: workbook cell-for-cell, five-question form structure, event identity, and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 2.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask, specify:
- Dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore` (read-only), or `coder` (write-capable).
- Whether the subtask is independent of its siblings (parallelizable) or must wait for another subtask's output.

TASK (as given by the user):
1. Look at all products in the WooCommerce store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.
2. Create a Google Form titled "Product Quality Improvement Survey" with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.
3. Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx (in the workspace: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace) with a sheet called "Review Summary" that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns Product_Name (truncated to 60 characters), Avg_Rating (rounded to 2 decimals), Review_Count, and Category (first category name from each product). Sort by Avg_Rating ascending. Add a second sheet called "Stats" with Metric and Value rows for: Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (product name truncated to 40 characters), and Avg_Rating_Overall (average rating across all reviewed products rounded to 2 decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, NOT spreadsheet formulas.
4. Schedule a calendar event on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm, title "Product Quality Review Meeting".
5. Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject "Product Quality Alert - Review Required" mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

CONTEXT:
- Tools available: WooCommerce MCP (products, product reviews, etc.), Google Forms MCP, Excel MCP, Google Calendar MCP, Email MCP, local python execution, and local file tools.
- The plan should consider: how to gather product review data (products + their reviews/ratings), how to compute average ratings and handle ties, how the Excel file should be structured, and verification steps for the form, excel, calendar, and email outputs.
- Workspace path: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace

Deliverable: A concise ordered subtask list with dispatch decision and dependency notes for each step. Note any risks (e.g., review data availability, tie-breaking, timezone for calendar event).
Plan product review analysis task

You are a coder sub-agent with access to WooCommerce MCP tools, local file tools, and python execution. Your job: compute a product review analysis for a WooCommerce store and save the results to a JSON file in the workspace. Do NOT create the form/excel/calendar/email — just compute and save data.

WORKSPACE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace

STEPS:
1. Read the full product list from this saved file (JSON array of WooCommerce product objects):
   /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/.tool_results/mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list-call_01_yi77R74EA0cj51KHUXuB0277-796012c1-7547-4700-9585-cb3f7da781f6.txt
   If the file is large, read it in chunks with the Read tool (it has an output_path / pagination). Alternatively, re-fetch products via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list (perPage=100, page=1) and ALSO fetch page=2 to confirm whether more products exist (stop when a page returns empty). For each product capture: id, name, average_rating, rating_count, categories[0].name (first category name; may be empty string if none).

2. Fetch ALL approved customer reviews via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list with status="approved", perPage=100, starting at page=1, incrementing page until an empty page is returned. For each review capture: product_id, rating. (Expected total ~396 reviews, ~4 pages.)

3. Compute (use python via mcp__local__python_execute or your own logic; you may write a python script file in the workspace if helpful):
   - For each product that has at least one approved review:
     - review_count = number of approved reviews for that product
     - avg_rating = mean of the ratings of those approved reviews, rounded to 2 decimals (use Python round())
     - category = first category name from the product object
   - IMPORTANT: cross-check computed avg_rating/review_count against the product's average_rating and rating_count fields; if the computed values are consistent use them. Report any discrepancies in your summary.
   - Only include products with >=1 approved review (reviewed products).

4. Sort all reviewed products by: (a) avg_rating ascending, (b) review_count descending (more reviews preferred on ties), (c) product id ascending (final deterministic tie-break).
   - The five lowest-rated products = the first 5 in this sorted order. Record their FULL names (untruncated), avg_rating, review_count, category.

5. Compute stats:
   - total_products_reviewed = number of reviewed products
   - lowest_rated_product = full name of the #1 product in the sorted order (also compute its 40-char truncation: name[:40])
   - avg_rating_overall = mean of the per-product avg_rating values across ALL reviewed products, rounded to 2 decimals. (If you judge a different interpretation more appropriate — e.g. mean of all individual ratings — report both values in your summary and clearly state which you used in the JSON.)

6. Truncation helper: Product_Name for the excel sheet = name truncated to 60 chars (name[:60], plain character truncation, NO ellipsis). Store both truncated and full names in the JSON.

7. Save ALL results to: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/analysis_results.json
   JSON structure:
   {
     "reviewed_products": [ {"product_id": int, "name": full, "name_60": truncated to 60, "avg_rating": float(2dp), "review_count": int, "category": str} ... ],  // in the sorted order (ascending avg_rating)
     "top5_lowest": [ {"product_id": int, "name": full, "avg_rating": float(2dp), "review_count": int, "category": str} ... ],  // first 5 of sorted order
     "stats": {
       "total_products_reviewed": int,
       "lowest_rated_product": full name,
       "lowest_rated_product_40": name[:40],
       "avg_rating_overall": float(2dp),
       "avg_rating_overall_all_individual_ratings": float(2dp)  // alternate interpretation for reference
     }
   }

8. Return in your final summary: the 5 lowest-rated product names (full) with their avg_rating and review_count, total_products_reviewed, lowest_rated_product (truncated 40), avg_rating_overall, and the path to analysis_results.json. Also mention any discrepancies between computed ratings and WooCommerce's average_rating/rating_count fields.
Compute product review analysis

You are a coder sub-agent. Create an Excel workbook file at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx

INPUT DATA: Read /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/analysis_results.json — it contains:
- "reviewed_products": list of objects, ALREADY SORTED by avg_rating ascending (with ties broken by review_count descending then product_id ascending). Each has: product_id (int), name (full), name_60 (name truncated to 60 chars), avg_rating (float, 2dp), review_count (int), category (str, first category name).
- "stats": {"total_products_reviewed": int, "lowest_rated_product": str, "lowest_rated_product_40": str (40-char truncation), "avg_rating_overall": float 2dp, ...}

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Use the Excel MCP tools (mcp__excel__*):
   - mcp__excel__create_workbook with filepath = the path above
   - Determine the default sheet name (via mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata) and rename it to "Review Summary" (mcp__excel__rename_worksheet).
   - Sheet "Review Summary": write header row ["Product_Name", "Avg_Rating", "Review_Count", "Category"] at A1, then one row per reviewed product (in the given sorted order) with values: name_60, avg_rating, review_count, category. Use mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel (data = list of rows as lists, start_cell "A1").
   - Add a second worksheet "Stats" (mcp__excel__create_worksheet), then write header ["Metric", "Value"] and rows:
       ["Total_Products_Reviewed", stats.total_products_reviewed]
       ["Lowest_Rated_Product", stats.lowest_rated_product_40]
       ["Avg_Rating_Overall", stats.avg_rating_overall]
     Use mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel.
2. CRITICAL: All numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) must be written as LITERAL NUMBERS (Python int/float), NOT as spreadsheet formulas (no strings starting with "=", no TEXT values for numbers). avg_rating values are already rounded to 2 decimals in the JSON — write them as floats (e.g., 3.5, 3.71, 4.0).
3. VERIFY after writing: call mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata on the file and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel for both sheets (Review Summary first ~5 rows and last ~2 rows; Stats full). Confirm: sheet names exactly "Review Summary" and "Stats", correct headers, 82 data rows in Review Summary (83 with header), numbers are numeric (not strings/formulas), ascending order of Avg_Rating, and the Stats values are correct.

Report back: confirmation the file was created at the exact path, the number of rows written, the read-back verification results (sheet names, headers, first few rows, stats rows, and confirmation that numeric cells are literal numbers), and the exact file size/path. Do NOT create any other files.
Create Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx
